plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, milk-white bells with delicate green-marked inner petals push through frost and leaf litter in woodlands, churchyards and gardens. They often form drifts that look like a late dusting of snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, and sometimes earlier in mild winters
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein and contain galantamine, a compound that has inspired a medicine used for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant, five-petaled blossoms open on bare, gnarled branches while cold air still lingers. The scent is sweet and spicy, and each flower is a small pale-pink cup. Ume groves are a much-loved sign that winter is turning toward spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, typically January to February
plants.location: Japan, China and temperate East Asia, as well as mild gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms, and in East Asian art it symbolizes perseverance because it flowers through the cold.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry rose-like blooms, from single cups to dense formal doubles, against dark leaves. In mild-winter gardens they are a showy burst of color in the coldest months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring, with many cultivars at peak in February
plants.location: Southeastern United States gardens, and its native Japan and Korea
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems lift round clusters of funnel-shaped, blue-violet flowers above arching strap-like leaves. In the height of southern summer they make a vivid, long-lasting display.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, December to February
plants.location: Eastern Cape, South Africa, and Southern Hemisphere gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
